title: 3D Feuerbach analogue for tetrahedra (Murakami / Court / Mannheim)

problemStatement.formal: Identify and formalize the correct 3D analogue of Feuerbach's theorem: a sphere associated to every (orthocentric) tetrahedron that is internally tangent to the insphere and externally tangent to the four exspheres.
problemStatement.plain: Feuerbach's theorem (2D) states that the incircle of a triangle is tangent to its nine-point circle. The 3D analogue is a classical open formalization target. Several natural candidate spheres have been refuted at the orthocentric tetrahedron T0 = ((2,0,0),(0,3,0),(0,0,6),(0,0,0)) by closed-form symbolic computation; the correct sphere appears in Murakami (1952) and Court (1934) but uses face circumsphere/circumcircle data rather than vertex-centroid combinations. This entry seeds the literature survey and formalization.
whyMatters: Closes the open question left by sister entry feuerbachs-theorem-oq-02-incomplete-01, where three natural candidate spheres were ruled out at T0
Adds a 3D classical-geometry result to the gallery (Mathlib 3D sphere tangency is sparse)
Builds on the 743-line coordinate infrastructure already in FeuerbachsTheoremOQ02.lean (Tetrahedron, OrthocentricTetrahedron, circumcenter, edge-midpoints, insphere/exspheres)

proven: 2D Feuerbach theorem formalized in FeuerbachsTheorem.lean and FeuerbachsTheoremOQ05.lean (inversive proof)

S1 (2026-06-13) refutation of the Feuerbach-sphere-of-the-first-kind tangency at T0: the homothetic sphere center (3G - O)/2 = G/2 = (1/4, 3/8, 3/4), radius R/2 = 7/4, has dist^2 to the incenter I = ((18 - 3 sqrt 14)/11)(1,1,1) equal to 0.2099, whereas (R/2 - r)^2 = 1.2862 — not internally tangent (and 0.2099 != (R/2 + r)^2 = 5.598, not externally tangent). S1 literature confirmation: classical Monge point M = 2G - O (Encyclopedia of Mathematics); Feuerbach sphere of the first kind = homothety (G, -1/2) of the circumsphere => center (3G - O)/2, radius R/2; the genuine 3D tangency analogue is Grace's theorem (a Poncelet-type closure), not a single sphere tangent to the insphere

S4 (DONE, 2026-06-13, build-free closed-form, hand-verified exactly): the EIGHT tangent spheres of T0 = (A=(2,0,0),B=(0,3,0),C=(0,0,6),D=(0,0,0)) solved in closed form over Q(sqrt 14). Centres are rho*(ex,ey,ez), ei in {+/-1}, with rho = 6/(s -/+ sqrt 14) where s = 3ex+2ey+ez; the 8 with rho>0 are: [1] INSPHERE (+,+,+) rho=(18-3 sqrt 14)/11; [2] D-EXSPHERE/beyond ABC (+,+,+) rho=(18+3 sqrt 14)/11; [3] C-EXSPHERE/beyond z=0 (+,+,-) rho=6/(4+sqrt 14); [4] roof (+,+,-) rho=6/(4-sqrt 14); [5] B-EXSPHERE/beyond y=0 (+,-,+) rho=6/(2+sqrt 14); [6] roof (+,-,-) rho=6/sqrt 14=3 sqrt 14/7; [7] A-EXSPHERE/beyond x=0 (-,+,+) rho=6/sqrt 14; [8] roof (-,+,-) rho=6/(sqrt 14-2). Classification 1 insphere + 4 exspheres + 3 roof matches Grace. The (+,+,+) sign pattern has the two rho-branches [1],[2] => homothety pair with centre D=origin (D lies on the three faces x=y=z=0).

S4 (DONE, 2026-06-13): GRACE SPHERE for the D-pair (insphere [1] + D-exsphere [2]) computed and verified EXACTLY. It is the sphere through the opposite-face vertices A,B,C with centre Q = (20/11, 45/22, 36/11) = (40,45,72)/22 and radius R_Theta = 85/22 — BOTH RATIONAL (the sqrt 14 cancels). Derivation: circle ABC has circumcentre P0=(5/14,15/14,39/14), circumradius^2=2275/196; spheres through it are Q(t)=P0+t*(3,2,1)/sqrt 14, and tangency to the insphere forces t=75 sqrt 14/154, whereupon the sqrt 14 cancels in Q=P0+(75/154)(3,2,1). Exact tangency checks: |Q-I|^2 = (2905+588 sqrt 14)/484 = ((49+6 sqrt 14)/22)^2 = (R_Theta - rho_in)^2 (internal); |Q-E|^2 = (2905-588 sqrt 14)/484 = ((49-6 sqrt 14)/22)^2 = (R_Theta - rho_Dex)^2 (internal). So the Grace sphere contains BOTH the insphere and the D-exsphere internally tangent — the genuine positive 3D Feuerbach (Grace) statement at T0, ready to transcribe to Lean.

ORIENT (2026-06-13, S1 — literature survey via web): The 'no web access' blocker from S0 was resolvable; a focused survey was completed. (i) The Encyclopedia of Mathematics ('Tetrahedron, elementary geometry of the') CONFIRMS the classical Monge point M = 2G - O ('the centroid is the middle point of the line segment connecting the circumcentre and the point of Monge') — so the file's mongePoint = 4G - 3O is definitively non-standard. (ii) It defines the Feuerbach sphere of the FIRST kind as the image of the circumsphere under the central stretching (homothety) with centre G and ratio -1/2; hence centre (3G - O)/2 and radius R/2 — the exact 3D analogue of the 2D nine-point circle (whose 2D centre (3G - O)/2 and radius R/2 give Feuerbach's theorem). The Monge point is the external centre of similitude of the circumsphere and this first-kind sphere. The SECOND-kind sphere (Euler sphere, orthocentric tetrahedra only) is centred at G and cuts each face in its nine-point circle. (iii) NEW REFUTATION (computed this iteration): the first-kind sphere (centre (3G - O)/2, radius R/2) is NOT tangent to the insphere at T0 — dist^2((3G-O)/2, I) = 0.2099 while (R/2 - r)^2 = 1.2862 (a fourth refuted candidate; note (3G-O)/2 = G/2 here because O = 2G at the trirectangular T0). (iv) MAIN REORIENTATION: the genuine 3D Feuerbach theorem is GRACE'S THEOREM — for a pair of neighbouring tangent spheres S, T of a tetrahedron there is a unique sphere Theta passing through the three vertices on the face-plane separating S and T and tangent (both-internally or both-externally) to S and T; it is Poncelet-related and implies Laguerre's theorem / the Euler-Chapple formula. Refs: Grace's theorem exposition in The American Mathematical Monthly 127(10) (2020), 'Tangent Spheres of Tetrahedra and a Theorem of Grace'; arXiv:2301.00731 'Feuerbach's and Poncelet's theorems meet in space'; Egervary (1950) 'On the Feuerbach spheres of an orthocentric simplex', Acta Math. Hungar. 1:5-16. CONCLUSION: there is no single canonical sphere tangent to the insphere of a general tetrahedron (the naive analogue is false); the right targets are either (a) the homothetic first-kind sphere as a face-INCIDENCE result, or (b) Grace's theorem as the true tangency analogue.

DECOMPOSE (2026-06-13, S2-S3 — Grace statement retrieved + target fixed): S2 resolved the S1 'primary sources not retrievable' blocker via web (arXiv:2301.00731 HTML + AMM 2020 abstract/metadata). PRECISE GRACE STATEMENT (Grace 1897; Thm 2.1 of arXiv:2301.00731): the EIGHT tangent spheres of a tetrahedron ABCD (= spheres tangent to all four face-PLANES, i.e. the affine hulls of the faces) partition into FOUR pairs, each pair homothetic with centre a vertex (e.g. D); for each pair there is a sphere passing through the three vertices A,B,C of the opposite face and tangent to both members. This is equivalent to the 'neighbouring tangent spheres separated by exactly one face-plane' form. The eight tangent spheres = 1 insphere + 4 exspheres (one per face) + 3 'roof'/midspheres (each touching two face-planes externally). KEY: Maehara & Martini (AMM 127(10):897-910, 2020) prove Grace ELEMENTARILY for the TRIRECTANGULAR tetrahedron, and T0 is exactly trirectangular (mutually perpendicular edges DA,DB,DC at D) — so the whole theorem is checkable in explicit coordinates over Q(sqrt 14), avoiding Mathlib's sparse 3D-tangency layer. S3 DECISION: formalize target (b) Grace at T0 (then general trirectangular), NOT the first-kind face-incidence (a). DERIVED SEED (analytic, build-free, NOT machine-checked): with faces x=0,y=0,z=0 and 3x+2y+z=6 (|n|=sqrt 14), every tangent-sphere centre is rho*(ex,ey,ez), ei in {+/-1} (the three coordinate-plane distances force |x|=|y|=|z|=rho), with |rho*(3ex+2ey+ez) - 6| = sqrt(14)*rho. The interior branch ex=ey=ez=+1 gives rho = 6/(6+sqrt 14) = (18-3 sqrt 14)/11 and centre rho*(1,1,1) — which REPRODUCES the tracker's incenter I and inradius r, validating the system. Spheres sharing a sign pattern (ex,ey,ez) lie on a ray through D=origin, so the two rho-branches of each linear equation form a homothety pair with centre D, and Grace's sphere for that pair passes through A,B,C (the face opposite D) — the construction is now fully concrete at T0 and ready to state in Lean once Docker returns.

ACT/SYNTHESIS (2026-06-13, S7 - DONE, build-free, generalised to ALL trirectangular tetrahedra; symbolically + numerically verified exactly): generalised the S4 T0 result to an arbitrary trirectangular tetrahedron D=(0,0,0), A=(a,0,0), B=(0,b,0), C=(0,0,c) (mutually perpendicular legs a,b,c>0 at D). Write sigma=a+b+c, s=1/a+1/b+1/c, n=sqrt(1/a^2+1/b^2+1/c^2). The three coordinate-plane tangencies force every tangent-sphere centre to be rho*(ex,ey,ez), ei in {+/-1}; the (+,+,+) homothety pair (centre D) is the insphere I and the D-exsphere E with rho_in=1/(s+n), rho_Dex=1/(s-n). Rationalising (s^2-n^2 = 2 sigma/(abc)) gives rho_in=(ab+bc+ca - sqrt(a^2 b^2+b^2 c^2+c^2 a^2))/(2 sigma) and rho_Dex=(ab+bc+ca + sqrt(a^2 b^2+b^2 c^2+c^2 a^2))/(2 sigma). MAIN RESULT (Grace sphere through A,B,C tangent internally to BOTH I and E): CENTRE Theta=((a+b)(a+c), (a+b)(b+c), (a+c)(b+c))/(2 sigma), RADIUS R=(a^2+b^2+c^2+ab+bc+ca)/(2 sigma), BOTH RATIONAL in a,b,c (the surd cancels). Exact tangency identities: |Theta-I|=R-rho_in=(a^2+b^2+c^2 + sqrt(a^2 b^2+b^2 c^2+c^2 a^2))/(2 sigma) and |Theta-E|=R-rho_Dex=(a^2+b^2+c^2 - sqrt(a^2 b^2+b^2 c^2+c^2 a^2))/(2 sigma), both positive => both internal. PROOF of simultaneous tangency: pass the sphere through A,B,C via the one-parameter pencil x^2+y^2+z^2+Dx+Ey+Fz+G=0 with D=-(a^2+G)/a, E=-(b^2+G)/b, F=-(c^2+G)/c (free parameter G); impose internal tangency to the insphere and square to eliminate R - the resulting equation in n splits into an even part and an odd part, the ODD part is IDENTICALLY ZERO, and the even part yields the unique G=abc/sigma independent of sign(n). Since n -> -n swaps the insphere (s+n) and the D-exsphere (s-n), the SAME Grace sphere is simultaneously tangent to both, and the surd cancellation forces Theta, R rational. SANITY: at T0 (a,b,c)=(2,3,6) this returns Theta=(40,45,72)/22, R=85/22, rho_in=(18-3 sqrt 14)/11, rho_Dex=(18+3 sqrt 14)/11 - exactly the S4 values. Verified symbolically (sympy: odd-in-n part = 0; G=abc/(a+b+c); factored Theta and R as above) and numerically to ~1e-15 over five triples including the irrational (1.5,2.7,4.1). This is the publishable positive 3D Feuerbach (Grace) theorem for the entire trirectangular family (cf. Maehara & Martini, AMM 127(10):897-910, 2020). Only the Lean transcription (S8) remains, Docker-gated.

File's `mongePoint = 4G - 3O` is non-standard. Classical convention (Coxeter; Altshiller-Court 'Modern Pure Solid Geometry'): M = 2G - O (reflection of O through G). Verified at T0 by Monge plane intersection: classical M coincides with the orthocenter D = (0,0,0), file's M does not.

For an orthocentric tetrahedron, the orthocenter H exists and equals the classical Monge point M = 2G - O. Thus the file's N24 = 2G - O = H is the classical orthocenter (a meaningful point), even though the file's *labeling* of M is non-standard.

Edge midpoints of any orthocentric tetrahedron lie on a sphere centered at G with squared radius (|AC|^2 + |BD|^2)/16 = (|AB|^2 + |CD|^2)/16 = (|AD|^2 + |BC|^2)/16. For T0 this evaluates to 49/16 = (R/2)^2. This is a real classical fact — but the corresponding sphere is not the Feuerbach analogue.

The face centroid of BCD in T0 lies at squared distance 9/16 from G, while (R/3)^2 = 49/36; hence the (G, R/3) sphere does NOT pass through face centroids in general. The phrase 'twelve-point sphere with center G and radius R/3' (folklore) needs careful re-examination — it may apply only to specific tetrahedron classes (regular? equifacial?).

Refutation calculation pattern: at T0, the field Q[sqrt 14] separates candidate tangencies cleanly because R = 7/2 (rational), I has the form (k - m sqrt 14)/n * (1,1,1) (single irrational direction), so dist^2 and (radius - r)^2 differ in the sqrt 14 coefficient, making symbolic comparison straightforward.

S1: The classical Monge point M = 2G - O is CONFIRMED by the Encyclopedia of Mathematics ('the centroid is the middle point of the line segment connecting the circumcentre and the point of Monge'). The file's mongePoint = 4G - 3O is non-standard and should be corrected/renamed.

S1: The Feuerbach sphere of the FIRST kind is the image of the circumsphere under the homothety (G, -1/2): center (3G - O)/2, radius R/2 — the exact 3D analogue of the 2D nine-point circle (which has center (3G - O)/2 and radius R/2). The Monge point is the external center of similitude of the circumsphere and this sphere. The SECOND-kind / Euler sphere (orthocentric tetrahedra only) is centered at G and cuts each face in its nine-point circle.

S1: The first-kind sphere is NOT tangent to the insphere at T0 (refuted this iteration). Combined with the three S0 refutations, NO naive homothetic/centroid sphere is tangent to the insphere of a general tetrahedron. This is expected: the true 3D Feuerbach result is Grace's theorem, a Poncelet-type closure relating tangent spheres, not a lone insphere-tangent sphere.

S1: Grace's theorem (the genuine 3D Feuerbach theorem): for a pair of neighbouring tangent spheres S, T of a tetrahedron there is a unique sphere Theta passing through the three vertices on the face-plane separating S and T, tangent to both S and T (both internally or both externally). It implies Laguerre's theorem and generalises the Euler-Chapple formula; it is intimately tied to the Poncelet closure theorem (arXiv:2301.00731).

S2: Grace 1897 homothety-pairs form (Thm 2.1 of arXiv:2301.00731): a tetrahedron has exactly EIGHT tangent spheres (= 1 insphere + 4 exspheres + 3 'roof' midspheres), partitioned into four pairs homothetic with centre a vertex; each pair's Grace sphere passes through the three vertices of the opposite face and is tangent to both. Equivalent to the neighbouring-spheres form.

S2: Maehara & Martini, AMM 127(10):897-910 (2020), give the elementary proof in the TRIRECTANGULAR case. Since T0 is trirectangular this is the right route: it keeps everything in explicit coordinates over Q(sqrt 14) and avoids the missing Mathlib 3D-tangency / face-circumsphere infrastructure entirely.

S3 (derived, build-free, NOT machine-checked): the 8 tangent spheres of T0 have centres rho*(ex,ey,ez), ei in {+/-1}, with the single scalar equation |rho*(3ex+2ey+ez) - 6| = sqrt(14)*rho (the three coordinate planes force |x|=|y|=|z|=rho; the slanted face 3x+2y+z=6 gives the rest). Interior branch (+,+,+) yields rho=(18-3 sqrt 14)/11 and centre rho*(1,1,1), reproducing the known incenter/inradius — a self-check that the sign system is correct.

S3: same-sign-pattern spheres are collinear with D=origin, so each sign pattern's two rho-branches are a homothety pair with centre D; Grace's sphere for such a pair passes through A,B,C. This concretely realises Grace's '(homothetic with centre D) + (sphere through opposite face's 3 vertices)' at T0 in closed form.

S4 (KEY RESULT): the Grace sphere of the D-pair has RATIONAL centre (40,45,72)/22 and RATIONAL radius 85/22 even though the incenter, D-exsphere centre, and both tangency radii live in Q(sqrt 14). This rationality is the 3D analogue of the 2D nine-point centre being a simple rational combination of triangle data, and makes the eventual Lean proof a pure ring identity once sqrt 14 is introduced as a variable s with s^2=14.

Because n->-n maps insphere<->D-exsphere, the SAME sphere is tangent to both - a clean coordinate proof of Grace's theorem for the trirectangular family, exactly the Maehara-Martini (AMM 2020) elementary route.
